name: SiteTree
canonicalInstance: /site.json relative to the active WebEngine instance root
purpose: provide one human-editable canonical authority for the public site hierarchy and deterministic derived projections

nodeSemantics.id: canonical globally unique node identity inside one SiteTree instance
nodeSemantics.label: canonical public label for the node
nodeSemantics.path: optional globally unique public path when the node is addressable
nodeSemantics.children: optional ordered child SiteTree nodes; runtime canonical snapshot represents a leaf as an empty children array

runtimeValidation: a node contains only id, label, path and children
id is required, trimmed by construction and matches [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*
label is required and is a non-empty trimmed string
path is optional; when present it is a non-empty trimmed absolute public path beginning with /
path contains no query or fragment component
ids are globally unique inside one SiteTree instance
paths are globally unique among addressable nodes inside one SiteTree instance
children is an array when present
cycles and reused node objects are rejected
validation does not normalize, repair or infer missing authority

runtimeIndex.snapshot: createSiteTreeIndex creates an isolated immutable runtime snapshot from validated instance data
runtimeIndex.unknown: a syntactically valid unknown id/path resolves to null
runtimeIndex.normalization: resolver does not lowercase, append slashes, remove slashes or otherwise normalize lookup identity

loader.failure: load/parse/validation failure rejects; no fallback hierarchy is invented

rules: site.json is instance data at <instance-root>/site.json and must not live under <instance-root>/lib/webengine/
SiteTree is the only canonical public hierarchy authority
Navigation, breadcrumbs and sitemap are derived from SiteTree
derived projections may be duplicated; hierarchy authority may not
public means exposed or addressable and does not imply anonymous access
public topic architecture and technical/runtime ownership are separate layers
API and service routing are separate machine-interface concerns and must not be inferred from SiteTree
invalid or ambiguous SiteTree data must not be repaired by inventing a second hierarchy
SiteTree must not infer authorization from hierarchy, paths or visibility
SiteTree node paths remain logical root paths and do not embed the active deployment prefix
